mainTopic: רבי מאיר's rule that one who goes against the owner's wishes is a גזלן, and a rented donkey that gets sick or is seized for government service
overview: The amud opens by finishing a line from the previous page: our משנה follows רבי מאיר, who holds that anyone who goes against the owner's wishes is called a גזלן. The גמרא asks where רבי מאיר says this. It tries his ruling about a dyer who used the wrong color, then a ברייתא about money collected for Purim. Each proof is pushed away, because each case has its own special reason. The third proof comes from a ברייתא about a poor person given a coin to buy a specific garment. Its stated reason, 'because he goes against the wishes of the owner,' proves רבי מאיר's rule. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about a rented donkey. It explains the word הבריקה as either an eye disease or worm rot, and tells a short story about worm rot on the king's clothing. Finally, רב and שמואל disagree about a donkey seized for government service. רב asks whether the donkey will come back, and שמואל asks which direction it was taken. A ברייתא challenges שמואל, and the גמרא answers for him in two ways using רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.title: Finishing the line: he is called a robber
steps.stepSummary: The last words of a statement from the previous page. Anyone who goes against the owner's wishes is called a גזלן.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Anyone who changes from the owner's wishes] is called a robber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the sentence it began on the previous page: according to רבי מאיר, someone who goes against the agreement is treated like a גזלן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being labeled a גזלן matters because a robber is responsible for the item even if something happens beyond his control. This label explains why the renter in our משנה is liable. The rest of this section asks where רבי מאיר actually says this.

keyTerms.meaning: a robber, someone who took what isn't his

phrases.english: is called a robber.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page: anyone who changes from the owner's wishes is called a robber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the statement from the previous page that our משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, one who changes from the owner's terms is treated as a גזלן.

steps.title: Which statement of רבי מאיר is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי מאיר says that someone who changes from the agreement is a גזלן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which ruling of רבי מאיר are we talking about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source: where do we see רבי מאיר holding this rule? This question sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not enough to say a view belongs to רבי מאיר. The גמרא wants to find the place where he actually says it, so the claim is solid.

phrases.english: Which [statement of] Rabbi Meir?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ruling of רבי מאיר shows that one who changes from the owner's terms is a גזלן?

steps.title: Suggested source: the dyer who used the wrong color
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רבי מאיר's ruling about a dyer who dyed wool the wrong color. רבי מאיר says the dyer pays the value of the wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is רבי מאיר's ruling about a dyer: we learned in a משנה that if someone gives wool to a dyer to dye it red and he dyes it black, or to dye it black and he dyes it red, רבי מאיר says the dyer pays him the value of his wool.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible source. In the dyer case, רבי מאיר makes the dyer pay for the wool, as if he had stolen it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dyer went against the owner's instructions. רבי מאיר treats him like a robber: the dyer keeps the wool and pays its original value. That seems to match the rule that anyone who changes from the owner's wishes is a גזלן.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say, if we suggest
as we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: If you say it is Rabbi Meir's [ruling] about a dyer,
as we learned in a Mishnah:
phrases.notes: This משנה is in בבא קמא 100b.

phrases.english: One who gives wool to a dyer
to dye it red for him
and he dyed it black,
[or to dye it] black and he dyed it red,
Rabbi Meir says:
He gives him the value of his wool.
phrases.notes: The dyer pays the owner. The dyer keeps the wool and pays what it was worth before dyeing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the question of which ruling is meant.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר holds that one who changes from the owner's terms is a גזלן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of the dyer: רבי מאיר says the dyer pays the value of the wool.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's opposing view in the dyer case
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה continues with רבי יהודה. The owner keeps the wool and pays the dyer the lower of two amounts: the dyer's expenses or the added value.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: if the added value is more than the expenses, the owner gives the dyer the expenses. If the expenses are more than the added value, he gives him the added value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the dyer משנה with רבי יהודה's view. רבי יהודה does not treat the dyer as a robber.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the wool stays with its owner. The dyer is paid, but only the lower amount, because he did not follow instructions. This contrast shows that רבי מאיר's ruling is the harsher one, which treats the dyer like a גזלן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If the increase in value is more than the expenses,
he gives him the expenses,
phrases.notes: Here the owner of the wool is paying the dyer.

phrases.english: and if the expenses are more than the increase in value,
he gives him the increase in value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation of the dyer משנה brought as a proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: the owner keeps the wool and pays the dyer the lower of the expenses or the added value.
steps.confusionAlert: Who pays switches between the two views. For רבי מאיר, the dyer pays the owner for the wool. For רבי יהודה, the owner pays the dyer for his work.

steps.title: Maybe the dyer case is different: he acquired the wool by changing it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Maybe the dyer pays for the wool only because dyeing it physically changed it, and that change made it his.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe there it is different, because the dyer acquired the wool through a physical change.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proposed source. The dyer case may have a different reason that has nothing to do with going against the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dyeing physically changes the wool. A physical change (שינוי מעשה) is a known way that someone who takes an item comes to own it. So רבי מאיר may make the dyer pay for the wool because he now owns it, not because anyone who changes from the owner's wishes counts as a robber. If that is the reason, the dyer case does not help explain our משנה about the renter.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do you know? how can you be sure?
a physical change made to an object

steps.whyThisMatters: This sends the גמרא looking for a different source for רבי מאיר's rule. It also teaches an important idea: a proof only works if the case has no other possible reason.

phrases.english: From where [do you know this]?
Perhaps it is different there,
because he acquired it through a physical change?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the dyer case as the source of רבי מאיר's rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the dyer משנה. It does not reject the claim that רבי מאיר holds the rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dyer's payment may come from acquiring the wool through שינוי מעשה, not from changing the owner's terms.
steps.whatToRemember: The dyer case is not a clear source for רבי מאיר's rule, because the physical change to the wool gives another reason why the dyer pays.

steps.title: A new proof from the Purim collection
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a new source for רבי מאיר: a ברייתא about money collected for Purim. It first quotes the opening opinion, which allows some flexibility.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי מאיר's source is the Purim collection. A ברייתא teaches: money collected for Purim is used for Purim, and money collected for a city goes to that city. We are not strict about it. They may buy calves, slaughter them and eat them, and whatever is left over goes into the general charity fund.
steps.whatsHappening: The dyer proof failed, so the גמרא brings a different case to show רבי מאיר's view. This step quotes the first opinion in the ברייתא and sets up רבי מאיר's opinion, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says Purim money goes to Purim, but we are not exact about it. The poor can enjoy a generous Purim meal, and any extra money goes to general charity. This lenient view sets up the contrast with the strict opinion quoted in the name of רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Money collected from the community to give the poor for Purim
Money collected for the poor of a specific city
We are not exact or strict about it

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּמִגְבַּת פּוּרִים,
phrases.english: Rather, this is the source for Rabbi Meir: the case of the Purim collection,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:
The Purim collection is for Purim.
The city collection is for that same city,
and we are not exacting in the matter.
phrases.notes: He means we don't limit the poor to the bare cost of the meal. They can celebrate generously.

phrases.english: Rather, they buy the calves
and slaughter and eat them,
and the leftover goes into the charity fund.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּמִגְבַּת פּוּרִים, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the dyer proof was rejected, this offers a new source for רבי מאיר's view.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר holds anyone who goes against the giver's or owner's wishes is treated like a גזלן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the Purim collection.

steps.title: The strict opinion in the name of רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with the strict view: Purim money may only be used for Purim, not even for a sandal strap. This view is quoted in the name of רבי מאיר, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: Purim money is for Purim. A poor person may not even buy a strap for his sandal with it, unless he made a condition in front of the people of the city. This is the view of רבי יעקב, who said it in the name of רבי מאיר. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and gives the strict opinion, which is said in the name of רבי מאיר. This is the part the גמרא wanted for its proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי מאיר's view, the poor person may not use Purim money for anything else, even something as small as a sandal strap. The only exception is if he made a condition in front of the townspeople. It looks like רבי מאיר forbids any change from what the giver intended.

keyTerms.meaning: A strap for his sandal, a tiny, cheap item
In front of the people of the city

steps.confusionAlert: The line starts with רבי אליעזר, but then says this is the view of רבי יעקב in the name of רבי מאיר. For the גמרא's proof, the key point is that this strict view comes from רבי מאיר.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מִגְבַּת פּוּרִים לְפוּרִים,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: The Purim collection is only for Purim,
and the poor person is not permitted
to buy from it even a strap for his sandal,
unless he made a condition
in front of the people of the city,
phrases.notes: The condition would be that he can use the money however he wants.

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Ya'akov, who said it in the name of Rabbi Meir.
And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is lenient.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מִגְבַּת פּוּרִים לְפוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted ברייתא and gives the strict view in the name of רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, Purim charity may not be used for anything else, even a sandal strap, unless a public condition was made.

steps.title: Rejecting the Purim proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. When someone gives money 'for Purim,' that is like a clear condition, so this case does not show a general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe there too, he gave the money with Purim in mind, and he did not give it for anything else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the Purim proof. It suggests that money given for Purim was clearly given only for that purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Collecting money 'for Purim' spells out its purpose, so it works almost like an explicit condition. Using it for something else breaks a clear condition. That does not prove רבי מאיר's general rule that any change from the owner's wishes makes someone a גזלן.

keyTerms.meaning: Maybe, perhaps; often opens a rejection
With the intention of, for the purpose of

phrases.english: Perhaps there too,
phrases.notes: Like the dyer case, this case may have its own special reason.

phrases.english: it was with Purim in mind that he gave it to him,

phrases.aramaic: אַדַּעְתָּא דְּמִידֵּי אַחֲרִינָא לָא יָהֵיב לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: but he did not give it to him for anything else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in steps 6-7.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Purim money is given for a clearly stated purpose, like an explicit condition. So the case does not prove a general rule about going against the owner's wishes.

steps.title: A third proof: a coin given for a robe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another ברייתא. רבי מאיר says a poor person given a coin to buy one garment may not buy a different one, because that goes against the giver's wishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here is רבי מאיר's source. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in the name of רבי מאיר: if someone gives a poor person a דינר to buy a robe, he may not buy a cloak with it. If it was for a cloak, he may not buy a robe with it, because he would be going against the giver's wishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third time to find רבי מאיר's source. This ברייתא uses the exact idea of going against the owner's wishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the poor person makes only a small switch, from one garment to another, and רבי מאיר still forbids it. His reason, מעביר על דעתו של בעל הבית, is the same idea as the statement from step 1. That makes this a much closer match than the dyer or Purim cases.

keyTerms.term: מַעֲבִיר עַל דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת
keyTerms.meaning: Goes against the wishes of the owner (here, the giver)

steps.whyThisMatters: The reason given here matches the wording of the original statement in step 1. This is why it is such a strong source for רבי מאיר's view.

phrases.english: Rather, this is the source for Rabbi Meir, as it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says in the name of Rabbi Meir:

phrases.aramaic: הַנּוֹתֵן דִּינָר לְעָנִי לִיקַּח לוֹ חָלוּק –
phrases.english: One who gives a dinar to a poor person to buy himself a robe,
he may not buy a cloak with it;
if it was for a cloak, he may not buy a robe with it,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּעֲבִיר עַל דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת.
phrases.english: because he goes against the wishes of the owner.
phrases.notes: Here the 'owner' is the person who gave the money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the Purim proof was rejected, the גמרא offers a third source.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר holds anyone who goes against the giver's or owner's wishes is treated like a גזלן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in the name of רבי מאיר about a coin given to a poor person for a specific garment.

steps.title: Maybe the poor person must obey only so the giver is not suspected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to reject the proof from the poor person's coin. Maybe he may not switch garments only because people would suspect the giver of not keeping his promise.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe that case is different, because people will come to suspect the giver. People will say: 'So-and-so said, I am buying clothing for this poor person, and he never bought it.' Or: 'He said, I am buying him a cloak, and he never bought it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 9. It offers a different reason why the poor person must buy exactly what he was told.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the poor person buys something else, people won't see him wearing the promised garment, and they will think the giver lied. So the rule might come from protecting the giver's good name, not from a general rule that changing someone's wishes is wrong. If so, this case would not prove רבי מאיר's general rule.

phrases.english: But perhaps it is different there
because they will come to suspect him,
phrases.notes: "Him" here is the giver of the coin, not the poor person.

phrases.english: for people will say,
So-and-so said:
I am buying clothing for such-and-such poor person,
and he did not buy it for him.
Alternatively: I am buying him a cloak,
and he did not buy it for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the poor person's coin, not רבי מאיר's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule could come from avoiding suspicion of the giver, not from a general rule about going against someone's wishes.

steps.title: The wording proves the rule: changing from the owner's wishes makes one a robber
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if suspicion were the reason, the ברייתא would say 'because of suspicion.' Since it says 'because he goes against the owner's wishes,' the proof stands: whoever goes against the owner's wishes is called a גזלן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the ברייתא say 'because of suspicion.' Why does it say 'because he goes against the wishes of the owner'? Learn from this that the reason is that he changed, and anyone who goes against the wishes of the owner is called a robber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the rejection of Step 10 by looking at the exact words of the ברייתא. It then states the rule as proven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave its reason clearly: going against the owner's wishes. It did not mention suspicion, so suspicion is not the reason. This shows רבי מאיר holds a general rule: changing from what the owner wanted makes a person a גזלן.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, let it teach (the text should have said so)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר, anyone who changes from what the owner or giver wanted is called a גזלן. The proof comes from the exact reason the ברייתא gives.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finally gives a solid source for רבי מאיר's rule after several proofs were pushed away in the earlier steps.

phrases.english: If so, let it teach: "Because of suspicion."

phrases.aramaic: מַאי: ״מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּעֲבִיר עַל דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת״ –
phrases.english: Why does it say: "Because he goes against the wishes of the owner"?
phrases.notes: The "owner" here is the person who gave the coin, as in the ברייתא from Step 9.

phrases.english: Learn from this: it is because he changed,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַמַּעֲבִיר עַל דַּעַת שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת
phrases.english: and anyone who goes against the wishes of the owner
is called a robber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the rejection in Step 10 and confirms the proof from Step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי מאיר holds that anyone who goes against the owner's wishes is called a גזלן.

steps.title: What does the word 'הבריקה' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה about a rented donkey that 'הבריקה' and asks what this word means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'One who rents a donkey and it הבריקה.' What does הבריקה mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: explaining a hard word in the משנה. This question sets up the answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that if a rented donkey gets sick this way, the owner does not have to replace it. To understand the case, we first need to know what kind of sickness the word describes.

keyTerms.meaning: And it became sick (exact meaning discussed here)

phrases.english: One who rents a donkey and it "hivrika,"
What is "vehivrika"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי מאיר discussion and opens a new topic about a word in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word והבריקה.

steps.title: Two meanings: an eye disease or worm rot
steps.stepSummary: Here in בבל they explained it as a white spot in the eye. רבא said it means worm rot (אבזקת).
steps.simpleTranslation: Here they translated it as 'light in the eye.' רבא said: worm rot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with two explanations of the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view says the donkey got a white spot on its eye that hurts its sight. רבא says it is a disease of worms. Either way, it is a sickness that makes the donkey unfit to work.

keyTerms.meaning: Light in the eye (a white spot on the eye)

phrases.english: Here they translated it: "light in the eye."
phrases.notes: "Here" means in בבל, where the גמרא was learned.

phrases.english: רבא said: worm rot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: והבריקה means either a white spot in the eye, or worm rot (רבא).

steps.title: The man who claimed he saw worm rot on the king's clothing
steps.stepSummary: A man said he saw worm rot on the king's clothing. They asked whether it was on silver (linen) or gold (wool) items. One version says he said silver and was killed; another says he said gold and was let go.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man said to people: 'I saw worm rot on the king's clothing.' They said to him: 'On what? On silver items or on gold items?' Some say he said 'silver items,' and they killed him. Some say he said 'gold items,' and they let him go.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story connected to the word אבזקת that רבא just used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Worms attack wool (the 'gold' items) but not linen (the 'silver' items). If he said linen, they knew he was lying, so they killed him. If he said wool, his claim was believable, so they let him go.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Silver' and 'gold' here are not metals. They are names for kinds of clothing: silver means linen and gold means wool.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to them:
There is worm rot on the king's clothing.
They said to him: On what?
On silver items, or on gold items?
phrases.notes: Silver items are linen clothes and gold items are woolen clothes. Worms eat wool, not linen.

phrases.english: Some say: he said on silver items,
and they killed him.
Some say: he said on gold items,
and they let him go.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲמַר לְהוּ: אַבְזְקָת בְּמֵילָתָא דְּמַלְכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a story about the word אבזקת from רבא's explanation in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story showing that worm rot attacks wool but not linen.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: a donkey seized for government service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה. If the rented donkey was seized for government service, the owner can say to the renter, 'Yours is in front of you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if the donkey was taken for government service, the owner tells the renter, 'Here is yours in front of you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a new line from the משנה. This sets up the argument between רב and שמואל that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא explained the word 'הבריקה.' Now it moves to the next case in the same משנה, where the government takes the donkey. In this case the משנה says the loss falls on the renter, and the owner does not have to replace the donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: Forced government service; officials seize an animal to work for them
'Yours is in front of you.' This is the owner's claim that he has no duty to replace the animal

phrases.english: Or if it was seized for government service,
he says to him: Here, yours is in front of you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from explaining the word 'הבריקה' to the next case in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a rented donkey is seized for government service, the owner may tell the renter 'yours is in front of you' and does not have to replace it.

steps.title: רב: this rule applies only to a temporary seizure
steps.stepSummary: רב limits the משנה. It applies only when the government will return the donkey. If the donkey is taken for good, the owner must provide a different donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: the משנה is talking only about a seizure where the donkey comes back. If it will not come back, the owner must give the renter another donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains that the משנה's rule has a limit. It covers only a seizure where the animal is later returned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the key question is whether the donkey is coming back. If it is, the renter can wait for it and the owner owes nothing more. If it is gone for good, it is like the donkey died, so the owner must replace it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They only taught this about.' A phrase that limits a rule to a narrower case
A seizure where the animal is later returned
To provide him with a replacement donkey

phrases.english: Rav said:
They taught this only about a seizure that returns.
But a seizure that does not return,
he is obligated to provide him a donkey.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּאַנְגַּרְיָא חוֹזֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה quoted in step 15 to a temporary seizure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner is exempt only if the seizure is temporary. If the seizure is permanent, he must replace the donkey.

steps.title: שמואל: it depends on the direction the donkey was taken
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says it makes no difference whether the seizure is temporary or permanent. What matters is whether the donkey was led off in the direction the renter was already traveling.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: whether or not the donkey will be returned, if it was taken along the road it was already going on, the owner says 'yours is in front of you.' If it was taken in a different direction, the owner must give another donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל disagrees with רב and gives a different way to divide the cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, returnable or not is not the test. The test is the direction of travel. If the officials are heading the way the renter wants to go, he can follow along and get his donkey back. If they head somewhere else, the owner must replace the donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whether... or...' Both cases are treated the same
In the direction it was already traveling

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two tests. רב asks 'Will the donkey come back?' שמואל asks 'Which way was it taken?'

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
Whether it is a seizure that returns
or a seizure that does not return,
if it was taken along the way it was going,
he says to him: Here, yours is in front of you.
But if it was not taken along the way it was going,
he is obligated to provide him a donkey.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: בֵּין אַנְגַּרְיָא חוֹזֶרֶת בֵּין אַנְגַּרְיָא שֶׁאֵינָהּ חוֹזֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב and limits the משנה by a different test.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner is exempt if the donkey was taken in the direction the renter was going. If it was taken another way, he must replace it, whether or not the seizure is permanent.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a seized donkey must always be replaced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict the משנה. It says that if the donkey died or was seized for government service, the owner must provide another donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a challenge: a ברייתא teaches that if a rented donkey got sick or went crazy, the owner says 'yours is in front of you.' But if it died or was seized by the government, the owner must give another donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that rules the opposite of the משנה on a seized donkey. This sets up a challenge to the views of רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה put the seized donkey in the same group as the sick donkey, where the owner owes nothing. The ברייתא puts the seized donkey in the same group as the dead donkey, where the owner must replace it. So the two sources clash, and each opinion must show how it explains the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They challenged.' This introduces a source brought against a statement

phrases.english: They challenged:
One who rents a donkey
and it got sick or went mad,
he says to him: Here, yours is in front of you.
If it died or was seized for government service,
phrases.notes: This is where the ברייתא differs from the משנה, which said the owner owes nothing for a seized donkey.

phrases.english: he is obligated to provide him a donkey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that clashes with the משנה, to test the opinions of רב and שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The views of רב and שמואל on how to read the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires the owner to replace a seized donkey, while the משנה exempts him. Each opinion must show how the two sources fit together.

steps.title: No problem for רב, but a problem for שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב can easily explain the clash. The משנה is about a temporary seizure, and the ברייתא is about a permanent one. שמואל does not use that test, so the ברייתא is a difficulty for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב there is no problem: here the donkey is returned, and there it is not. But for שמואל it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא fits רב's view but challenges שמואל's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads the משנה as a seizure where the donkey returns, so the owner owes nothing. He reads the ברייתא as a seizure where it does not return, so the owner must replace it. שמואל says returnable or not makes no difference, so he cannot use this split. The ברייתא, which says a seized donkey must always be replaced, now seems to argue with him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is fine for...' One view works, and the challenge is coming for the other
'Here... there...' Two sources are explained as talking about different cases
'But according to שמואל it is difficult'

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next step, where שמואל has to defend his opinion against the ברייתא.

phrases.english: It is fine according to Rav; it is not difficult:
Here, it is about a seizure that returns,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the משנה, where the owner owes nothing because the donkey comes back.

phrases.english: There, it is about a seizure that does not return.
phrases.notes: 'There' is the ברייתא, where the owner must replace the donkey.

phrases.english: But according to Shmuel it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sharpens the challenge from step 18 so that it targets שמואל only.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that whether the donkey returns makes no difference
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says a seized donkey must be replaced. Without רב's split between temporary and permanent seizure, שמואל cannot explain why the ברייתא disagrees with the משנה.

steps.title: A suggested way for שמואל to answer the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that שמואל could also settle the clash. The משנה would be about a donkey led off in the renter's direction, and the ברייתא about one led off in a different direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might say there is no difficulty for שמואל either. The משנה is a case where the donkey was taken along the route it was already going. The ברייתא is a case where it was taken in a different direction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer for שמואל, using his own 'direction' test to separate the משנה from the ברייתא. This is a suggestion that the גמרא is about to test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב settled the clash by splitting temporary seizure from permanent seizure. Here the גמרא tries the same kind of split for שמואל, using the direction the donkey was led. If the donkey went the renter's way, 'yours is in front of you.' If not, the owner must give another donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you would say': it introduces a suggested idea, which is often rejected right after
The route the donkey was already traveling, meaning the renter's direction

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא לִשְׁמוּאֵל נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: And if you would say: according to Shmuel too, it is not difficult:
here, it was taken along the route it was going,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the משנה, where the owner can say 'yours is in front of you.'

phrases.english: there, it was taken not along the route it was going.
phrases.notes: 'There' means the ברייתא, which says the owner must provide another donkey.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא לִשְׁמוּאֵל נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes for שמואל a split like the one רב used in step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting cases (אוקימתא) by direction of travel
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and ברייתא clash for שמואל
steps.terutzMaskana: Suggested: the משנה is about a donkey taken in the renter's direction, and the ברייתא is about one taken in another direction

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא shows the direction test belongs only to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion fails. The end of the ברייתא gives the direction test in the name of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, so the first opinion in the ברייתא must not use it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the end of the ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: if the donkey was taken along its route, the owner says 'yours is in front of you'; if not, he must provide a donkey. This shows that for the תנא קמא, direction makes no difference!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggested answer for שמואל by pointing to the last line of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the direction test were already built into the first opinion, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר would have nothing new to add. Since he adds it, the תנא קמא must say 'provide another donkey' in every case of seizure. So the ברייתא's main opinion still disagrees with שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: The later or last part of a teaching
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
'By implication': we can infer from this
It makes no difference to him

steps.confusionAlert: The direction test is not being rejected here. The point is only that, inside this ברייתא, it belongs to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and not to the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: But from the fact that the later part teaches:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
if it was taken along the route it was going,
he says to him: yours is in front of you,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו – חַיָּיב לְהַעֲמִיד לוֹ חֲמוֹר.
phrases.english: and if not, he must provide him a donkey.

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דִּלְתַנָּא קַמָּא לָא שָׁאנֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: This implies that for the first opinion it makes no difference!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer proposed in step 20
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested split by direction as a reading of the תנא קמא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The direction test is said by רבי שמעון בן אלעזר as his own view, which implies the תנא קמא does not hold it

steps.title: שמואל follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that he agrees with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, so it does not matter that the תנא קמא disagrees with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל can tell you: Isn't there רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who holds like me? I ruled like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for שמואל. He openly admits that the תנא קמא disagrees, but he sides with the תנא who agrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A אמורא may follow one תנא against another. So a ברייתא only troubles שמואל if no תנא supports him. Here רבי שמעון בן אלעזר does.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He would tell you': it introduces how the scholar would defend himself
Who stands with me, who holds like me

phrases.english: Shmuel can say to you:

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִי אִיכָּא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר דְּקָאֵי כְּווֹתִי?
phrases.english: Isn't there Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, who holds like me?

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר.
phrases.english: I spoke in line with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty that remained after step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Siding with one תנא against another
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's תנא קמא refutes שמואל
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, so a disagreeing תנא is no refutation

steps.title: The whole ברייתא is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view, with missing words filled in
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the entire ברייתא follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and is missing some words. Read correctly, it says that seizure obligates the owner only when the donkey is led off in a different direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you prefer, say the whole ברייתא is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's, and it is missing words. This is what it means: If someone rents a donkey and it became ill or went mad, the owner says 'yours is in front of you.' If it died or was seized for government service, he must provide a donkey. When is this so? When it was taken not along its route. But if it was taken along its route, he says 'yours is in front of you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer for שמואל. There is no disagreement in the ברייתא at all; it just needs to be read with some missing words added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first answer, the תנא קמא disagrees with שמואל. In this answer, the ברייתא speaks with one voice. For a seized donkey, the 'must provide a donkey' rule applies only when it was taken in a different direction, which is exactly שמואל's test. Now the ברייתא fully supports שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you want, say': it introduces a second, different answer
The text is missing words, and the גמרא fills them in
Forced government service, when the authorities seize an animal for work
'When is this said?': it introduces a limit on the rule just stated

steps.whatToRemember: For שמואל, what decides the seized-donkey case is direction. If the donkey was led off along the renter's route, 'yours is in front of you.' If not, the owner must provide another donkey. He can rely on רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, or read the whole ברייתא as following him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא tool: saying a text is missing words (חסורי מיחסרא) so that it fits an אמורא's view, instead of saying the תנאים disagree.

phrases.aramaic: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא כּוּלָּהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר הִיא,
phrases.english: If you prefer, say the whole of it is Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar,
and it is missing words, and this is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: הַשּׂוֹכֵר אֶת הַחֲמוֹר וְהִבְרִיקָה אוֹ נִשְׁתַּטֵּית,
phrases.english: One who rents a donkey and it became ill or went mad,
he says to him: yours is in front of you.
If it died or was seized for government service,
he must provide him a donkey.
When is this said?
phrases.notes: From here on is the part the גמרא says was missing from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: When it was taken not along the route it was going,
but if it was taken along the route it was going,
he says to him: yours is in front of you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא כּוּלָּהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to the difficulty from step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Filling in missing words in the ברייתא (חסורי מיחסרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא contains a תנא קמא who disagrees with שמואל
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole ברייתא is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view, and it limits the obligation to a donkey led off in a different direction, matching שמואל
